note: Alaska takes abuse reports by phone, email or fax, and says its hotline staff will answer questions about mandatory reporting and take all the required information over the phone - which is worth knowing if you are unsure whether what you have is enough to report. All the mental health licensing boards sit under one division, with a single investigations unit behind them.

civil_injury.summary: Two years from when the injury happened (when the claim 'accrued'). The same two years covers assault, battery, false imprisonment and negligence/personal injury.
civil_injury.quote: a person may not bring an action (1) for libel, slander, assault, battery, seduction, or false imprisonment, (2) for personal injury or death, or injury to the rights of another not arising on contract ... unless the action is commenced within two years of the accrual of the cause of action.
civil_injury.note: Alaska courts apply a common-law discovery rule to accrual in some cases; that is case law, not statute text, and was not verified here.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: The clock does not run while the injured person is under 18, but the extension cannot go more than two years past the 18th birthday. In practice, someone hurt as a minor has until age 20.
civil_minor_tolling.quote: if a person entitled to bring an action ... is at the time the cause of action accrues either (1) under the age of majority ... the time of a disability ... is not a part of the time limit ... the period ... is not extended in any case longer than two years after the disability ceases.
civil_minor_tolling.note: Subsection (c) separately excludes time before the eighth birthday; it is a leftover of the 1997 tort-reform limit on minority tolling (the Alaska Supreme Court struck that limit in Sands v. Green, 2007) and does not shorten (a). The special delayed-discovery rule in (b) is for sexual abuse only. No general statutory discovery rule for non-sexual abuse was found.

civil_government_claims.summary: No advance notice of claim is required to sue the State of Alaska in tort; the normal two-year deadline applies. But the State cannot be sued for claims arising out of assault, battery or false imprisonment (only negligence-type claims), so a survivor may need to sue the individual staff or a private contractor instead.
civil_government_claims.quote: A person or corporation having a contract, quasi-contract, or tort claim against the state may bring an action against the state ... However, an action may not be brought if the claim ... (3) arises out of assault, battery, false imprisonment, false arrest, malicious prosecution, abuse of process
civil_government_claims.note: No notice-of-claim statute for state or municipal tort suits was found in AS 09.50 or 09.65.070. Municipal immunity in § 09.65.070(d) covers discretionary functions but not intentional torts by name. Not confirmed whether any local charter adds a notice rule.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: Alaska has no separate felony 'physical child abuse' crime; physical abuse of a child is charged as assault (including third-degree assault for injuring a child under 12, or 12-15). Felony assault must be charged within 10 years of the offense. The clock is not paused until the child turns 18 for these non-sexual crimes.
criminal_child_abuse.quote: a person may not be prosecuted ... unless the indictment is found or the information or complaint is instituted not later than (1) 10 years after the commission of a felony offense in violation of AS 11.41.120 - 11.41.330 ... or (2) five years after the commission of any other offense.
criminal_child_abuse.note: Endangering the welfare of a child (AS 11.51.100) sits outside AS 11.41, so it falls under the five-year default. Time can stop running (up to 3 extra years) while the accused hides out of state (§ 12.10.040). Kidnapping has no limit (§ 12.10.010(a)(6)); custodial interference is within 11.41.300-.330 (10 years if a felony).

criminal_felony_assault.summary: Felony assault (first, second or third degree) must be charged within 10 years of the offense. Misdemeanor assault and other offenses: five years.
criminal_felony_assault.quote: not later than (1) 10 years after the commission of a felony offense in violation of AS 11.41.120 - 11.41.330 ... or (2) five years after the commission of any other offense.
criminal_felony_assault.note: Assault offenses are AS 11.41.200-11.41.230, inside the 11.41.120-.330 range. Time starts the day after the offense (§ 12.10.030).

channels.name: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Staffs and investigates for the Board of Professional Counselors, the Board of Psychologist and Psychological Associate Examiners and the Board of Social Work Examiners, and the boards discipline the licence.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor, psychologist, psychological associate or social worker in Alaska.
channels.how: File the complaint with the Division, which handles investigations for all three boards.
channels.mail: Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing, 550 W 7th Ave, Ste 1500, Anchorage, AK 99501-3567

channels.name: Alaska Office of Children's Services reporting hotline
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory report line for child abuse and neglect in Alaska.
channels.who_to_report: A child at an Alaska program.
channels.how: Call, email or fax. Staff will answer questions about mandatory reporting and take everything they need over the phone.
channels.note: If the problem is the Office of Children's Services itself rather than a program, there is a separate formal complaint process for that.

channels.name: Alaska residential child care facility licensing
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses Alaska's residential child care facilities against the state licensing regulations and investigates complaints that a facility has breached them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Alaska residential child care facility.
channels.how: Start from the Department's reporting hub, which sets out which body takes which kind of concern.
channels.phone_note: The Office of Children's Services line also takes concerns about licensed facilities.

channels.name: Disability Law Center of Alaska
channels.what_it_can_do: Alaska's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: An Alaska program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
